statement: Show that the coefficient of $x^{n}$ in the expansion of $(1-x)^{-1/2}$ is $\dfrac{(2n)!}{2^{2n}(n!)^{2}}$, and state the values of $x$ for which the expansion is valid.
solution: $(1-x)^{-1/2}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\dfrac{(-\tfrac12)(-\tfrac32)\cdots(-\tfrac{2n-1}{2})}{n!}(-x)^{n}$. The product of the $n$ negative half-integers equals $\dfrac{(2n)!}{2^{2n}n!}$ in magnitude (after collecting signs), giving coefficient $\dfrac{(2n)!}{2^{2n}(n!)^{2}}$. The expansion is valid for $|x|<1$.
